short: A booked party that never arrives.
metaDescription: A no-show is a confirmed reservation whose guests never arrive. It is one of the few losses that is entirely avoidable with a reminder.
definition: A no-show is a confirmed reservation whose guests never arrive. The table is held, turned away from walk-ins, and produces nothing — a direct loss of the revenue that seat could have earned.
bodyHtml:
Why No-Show matters

On a full Saturday, a handful of no-shows removes several thousand rupees of covers that were available and refused. It is one of the few losses that is entirely avoidable with a reminder.

No-Show formula

No-show rate % = No-shows ÷ Total reservations × 100

Multiply by average cover and party size to value the loss.

How No-Show works in practice

Confirm by message a few hours ahead, hold tables for a stated grace period, and track the no-show rate by source. Repeat offenders and particular booking channels usually account for most of it.

faq.question: Should I take a deposit?
faq.answer: For large parties and peak slots it is reasonable, and stating the policy at booking usually reduces no-shows on its own.

faq.question: How long should a table be held?
faq.answer: Fifteen to twenty minutes is common, provided the policy is communicated when the booking is made.

formula.note: Multiply by average cover and party size to value the loss.
